{"notes": "Visit 6 (8:00). Nobody spoke while I was there. Picture looks the same as before: the pale cluster at ~23-24, 8.5-9.3 on the upper tail is still disconnected, so the upper tail past the crossing will probably not topple. The belly line is still doubled around 19-22, 11-13. Neither problem has been fixed or mentioned in two visits. I still don't know who placed which domino, so I can't attribute anything to a person. Judge on the review answers and the result.

Sofia: Silent again. Earlier she claimed the crossing-to-upper-tail section, and the gap is in or next to it. She called the doubled joint 'fine' without checking. Earlier leadership and collaboration credit stands (clear split, reassured Jack). Execution is unproven and a concern. Ask what she placed last and whether she checked the gap.

Omar: Silent again. He offered earlier to nudge the off-to-side domino before the crossing; I can't confirm he did it or whether the pale cluster is his. Don't rate him on guesses. Ask him directly. Low visibility is a collaboration question mark, not evidence of poor work.

Hana: Took the crossing join, and the belly connects through it. Silent again. She never raised the issues. Ask what she placed and whether she saw the gap.

Jack: Inspector on the doubled joint. He cheered 'proper fish, great teamwork' earlier while the problems were visible. Inspection looks ineffective, though his warmth is real. Ask what he checked and what he told people.

Review: watch how far the dominoes fall. If the upper tail stalls at the gap, ask each person what they placed and who owned the gap."}
